title: Non-atomic case: resolved link boundary not equivariantly identified with the genuine slice frontier S(nu) for gluing

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Location.** `prop:induct` together with the assembly in `sec:global`.

**The gap (non-atomic refinement of q7-10).** For a non-atomic stratum, `prop:induct` builds a **resolved** link $\widehat L$ with only a *rational homology equivalence* $\widehat L\to L = S(V)/F$, and then fills $\widehat L$ to obtain $V_F$ with $\partial V_F=\widehat L$ (and $\partial W_F$ the corresponding cover).

But the global assembly in `sec:global` **deletes the cone neighborhood $N_F$ whose frontier is the genuine sphere bundle $S(\nu)$** (resp. its quotient $L_F$), and then glues in $R_F$ along $\partial R_F$. The text asserts "$\partial R_F = S(\nu)$ matching $\partial N_F$ $F$-equivariantly." For non-atomic strata this is **not justified**, because:
- the model's boundary is the **resolved** object $\widehat L$ (a surgered/modified link), whereas the frontier being matched is the **genuine** $S(\nu)$ (an honest sphere bundle on which $F$ acts with fixed points);
- a *rational homology equivalence* $\widehat L\to L$ is **not** an $F$-equivariant diffeomorphism, so it cannot be used to glue manifolds.

No explicit $F$-equivariant diffeomorphism $\partial W_F \cong_F S(\nu)$ is produced in the non-atomic case, so the pieces cannot be inserted in place of the excised cones.

**Fix.** Either (a) keep the boundary genuinely equal to $S(\nu)$ throughout the inductive resolution (resolve the *interior*, never the frontier), or (b) prove that the resolved boundary is $F$-equivariantly diffeomorphic to the genuine frontier. This is the non-atomic version of the interface condition tracked in q7-10.
